text:
The Rangers lost Igor Shesterkin to a season-ending knee injury on October 9, five games into the year, and they are 12-8-1 anyway. That's the story of their season so far, and it's a better one than it had any right to be.

Dylan Garand, a rookie who had been waived after camp, played 12 straight games while Joonas Korpisalo was out. Korpisalo returned on November 7 and has won his starts since, including a diving, stick-less save in Calgary that made highlight reels. The third option didn't work: James Reimer made one start, lasted a period, and his contract was terminated. Mike Sullivan now has two goalies he trusts, and the New York Post headline this week called it balance.

The skaters deserve credit. New York has taken 54% of the expected goals, a measure of chance quality, and has actually scored eight fewer goals than those chances say, so the offense has room to grow. Adam Fox and Vladislav Gavrikov (58% of the expected goals) anchor the back end, and the J.T. Miller line with Pavel Dorofeyev and Tye Kartye drives play at 64%, even though it has been outscored 7-4.

Our numbers give them a 66% chance at the playoffs. The worry is obvious: a tandem of a rookie and a journeyman for 60 more games, with no margin if either gets hurt.
headline: Rangers holding up without Shesterkin
